references.text: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams, which predict seven years of abundance followed by seven years of famine, corresponding to the seven fruitful years mentioned in verse 47.
Joseph advises Pharaoh to collect one-fifth of the harvest during the seven good years, directly anticipating the fruitful years described in verse 47.
Joseph gathers food during the seven years of abundance, and the grain was like the sand of the sea—a direct follow-up to the fruitful years described in verse 47.
After the seven years of abundance, the seven years of famine begin, confirming the prediction and actions taken during the seven fruitful years.
Joseph explains to his brothers that there have been two years of famine and five more remain, confirming the seven years of abundance followed by seven years of famine.
Psalm 105:16-17 refers to the famine and Joseph being sent ahead to Egypt, linking Joseph's role with the period of abundance and famine.
Prediction of seven years of abundance (41:29) and its actual fulfillment (41:47).
Describes respectively the content and conclusion of the seven years of abundance.
The plan to store food (41:36) and the actual abundance that made it possible (41:47).
